newsitem.title: POLAND: Striking Polish lignite mine head sent on leave.
newsitem.headline: Striking Polish lignite mine head sent on leave.

text.p: Polish treasury minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz on Monday sent the head of Poland's largest lignite mine, state-owned KWB Belchatow, on indefinite leave until demands for his dismissal by the striking mine were reviewed.
"I decided that the only possible solution was to send the head of the mine on indefinite leave until the matter is resolved," Pietrewicz told a news conference.

Last Friday, workers at Belchatow began reducing coal deliveries to Poland's largest power plant, demanding the dismissal of their director general whom they accuse of violating labour agreements and mismanagement.

The giant Belchatow plant, which supplies 25 percent of Poland's electricity, has no sources of coal other than the Belchatow mine and the cut in deliveries caused the shut-down of nine of of the powerplant's 12 blocks.
Energy-sector officials have said the strike could lead to power cuts and electricity imports if temperatures in Poland again fall well below zero.
Pietrewicz said he had set up a special committee to investigate the dispute at Belchatow, which will present its conclusions this week.
